test_m1 = '''"""Test m1: @memoize decorated function has .memory attribute; calling .invalidate_all() makes .memory empty; subsequent calls recompute."""

import pytest


def test_memoize_invalidate_all_exists():
    """The @memoize wrapper must expose an .invalidate_all method."""
    from funcy.calc import memoize

    @memoize
    def add(a, b):
        return a + b

    # This attribute must exist on the wrapper
    assert hasattr(add, "invalidate_all")


def test_memoize_invalidate_all_clears_memory():
    """Calling .invalidate_all() on a @memoize wrapper must clear its memory."""
    from funcy.calc import memoize

    call_count = [0]

    @memoize
    def multiply(a, b):
        call_count[0] += 1
        return a * b

    # Populate memory
    multiply(2, 3)
    assert len(multiply.memory) > 0

    # Invalidate all
    multiply.invalidate_all()

    # Memory must be empty after invalidation
    assert len(multiply.memory) == 0


def test_memoize_invalidate_all_triggers_recompute():
    """After .invalidate_all(), calling with the same args must recompute."""
    from funcy.calc import memoize

    call_count = [0]

    @memoize
    def subtract(a, b):
        call_count[0] += 1
        return a - b

    # First call populates cache
    r1 = subtract(10, 3)
    assert r1 == 7
    assert call_count[0] == 1

    # Second call uses cache
    r2 = subtract(10, 3)
    assert r2 == 7
    assert call_count[0] == 1

    # Invalidate all
    subtract.invalidate_all()

    # Third call must recompute
    r3 = subtract(10, 3)
    assert r3 == 7
    assert call_count[0] == 2


def test_memoize_invalidate_all_is_callable():
    """.invalidate_all() must be callable on the memoize wrapper."""
    from funcy.calc import memoize

    @memoize
    def identity(x):
        return x

    assert callable(identity.invalidate_all)
'''

with open("crucible_hidden/test_m1.py", "w") as f:
    f.write(test_m1)
